workLog.entry: Selected #3016 as the last ADR-needing issue per the owner mandate. Read the full issue and its acceptance criteria, including the mandatory calibration gate.

Grounded against real infra: the false-completion gate is a local 5s blocking PreToolUse hook that only checks external evidence; the eval scorer supports only REGEX/VERDICT fixture assertions; the session-log schema has no confidence field.

Ran the ADR Review Protocol: a multi-agent consensus debate on ADR-081 with the architect agent and a GPT-5.5 independent-thinker. Both concluded the blocking-hook design is unbuildable and the calibration circular. Recorded findings in .agents/analysis/ADR-081-confidence-elicitation-debate.md.

Wrote ADR-081: reject the blocking hook; reframe into an offline shadow study with external-only labels and a power-justified corpus, plus a recommended gate-hardening alternative and a WONTFIX option, for the owner to choose under User Sovereignty.
Addressed bot review on the ADR PR for #3016: set endingCommit to the work commit so it agrees with changesCommitted and the episode emits a commit event.
Removed 3 auto-generated retrospective files that an auto-staging hook swept into the ADR PR; they are scope creep on an atomic ADR change.
Bot review: corrected the ADR to say one GPT-5.5 pass (not two) and marked the ADR-080 cross-reference as a concurrent proposed sibling not yet on main.
Owner accepted ADR-081: shadow-study reframe accepted, blocking hook rejected (latency/cost). Flipped status proposed -> accepted and recorded the track-1 decision.

nextSteps: Owner chooses among the three tracks in ADR-081 (shadow study, gate hardening, or WONTFIX).
If gate hardening is chosen, implement evidence-after-last-edit in the false-completion gate.
